Company Overview

Apple Inc. is a technology company that designs, develops and markets consumer electronics, software and digital services. Its principal products include the iPhone, Mac computers, iPad tablets, Apple Watch, AirPods and other accessories. The company also develops operating systems and applications that support its hardware products.

Apple’s services business includes the App Store, Apple Music, Apple TV, Apple Arcade, Apple Fitness+, Apple News+, Apple Pay and iCloud. These services provide digital content, payments, cloud storage and subscription offerings across the company’s ecosystem of devices.

Founded in 1976, Apple is headquartered in Cupertino, California, and serves consumers, businesses, educational institutions and government customers worldwide. The company sells its products through its retail and online stores, third-party retailers, cellular carriers and other distribution partners.

Tim Cook has served as Apple’s chief executive officer since 2011. The company’s global operations include product development, software engineering, retail, customer support and a supply chain spanning multiple regions.

AAPL Stock Analysis - Frequently Asked Questions

Apple's stock was trading at $271.86 at the start of the year. Since then, AAPL stock has increased by 24.7% and is now trading at $338.98.

Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) released its quarterly earnings results on Thursday, July, 30th. The iPhone maker reported $2.02 earnings per share for the quarter, beating the consensus estimate of $1.89 by $0.13. The company's quarterly revenue was up 16.4% on a year-over-year basis.
Read the conference call transcript.

Shares of Apple split before market open on Monday, August 31st 2020.The 4-1 split was announced on Thursday, July 30th 2020. The newly issued shares were distributed to shareholders after the market closes on Friday, August 28th 2020. An investor that had 100 shares of stock prior to the split would have 400 shares after the split.

Apple's board initiated a share repurchase plan on Thursday, May 1st 2025, which permits the company to buy back $100,000,000,000 in outstanding shares, according to EventVestor. This means that the company could purchase up to 3.1% of its stock through open market purchases. Stock repurchase plans are typically a sign that the company's leadership believes its stock is undervalued.

The following companies are subsidiaries of Apple: Joby Aviation, Credit Kudos, AI Music, Paws Inc, Primephonic, SourceDNA, Vilynx, and others.

Apple's top institutional investors include Berkshire Hathaway Inc (1.56%), Bank of America Corp DE (0.88%), Legal & General Group Plc (0.72%) and UBS AM a distinct business unit of UBS ASSET MANAGEMENT AMERICAS LLC (0.71%). Insiders that own company stock include Arthur D Levinson, Timothy D Cook, Jeffrey E Williams, Katherine L Adams, Deirdre O'brien, Luca Maestri, Ben Borders, Jennifer Newstead, Chris Kondo and Kevan Parekh.
View institutional ownership trends.

Shares of AAPL stock can be purchased through any online brokerage account. Popular online brokerages with access to the U.S. stock market include Charles Schwab, E*TRADE, Fidelity, and Vanguard Brokerage Services.

Based on aggregate information from My MarketBeat watchlists, some other companies that Apple investors own include Meta Platforms (META), NVIDIA (NVDA), Tesla (TSLA), Broadcom (AVGO), SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Chevron (CVX).
